Gwil Stannard.narrative: I am the only mason and roofer in Cullet, and every roof in town is several shades of grey because of me. I patch what I can with slates from the shells, but there are more leaks than hours in the day, and I owe favours to half the town and they owe me. I mended the Cone's cracked band with Corvin Hollin, and I take slates from Mid Row 3 because nobody lives there to mind. My wife Cora grows flowers in a corner of glasshouse 4, and I know Oswin wants it back, but I keep out of that.
goals: Get every roof in town watertight before next winter
Collect the favours owed to me so I can call them in when I need help
Keep Cora happy and her flowers safe
Find a way to get more slates without stripping the shells bare
pastimes: Walking the Rows to spot a loose slate
Sitting at the wash-house wall with a cup
Gwil Stannard.calling: I love the feel of a roof coming right under my hands, and the look of a dry ceiling after a storm.
Gwil Stannard.mood: Tired but steady; there is always another roof.

relations.name: Cora Stannard
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps me level, and her flowers are the one thing I never argue about.

relations.name: Dolly Achterberg
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe her a favour for the Marver's roof; she never lets me forget it.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I patched her smokehouse roof and she has not called it in yet.

relations.name: Vessa Pontil
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: The Cone's band was a hard job; she owes me, but she is not quick to pay.

relations.name: Corvin Hollin
relations.label: workmate
relations.note: We mended the Cone together; he is a good man with a straight eye.

relations.name: Oswin Greave
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He wants Cora's corner, and I want him to leave it be.

relations.name: Pieter Achterberg
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play counters at the Marver and he always asks for peat, but he is good company.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: He keeps the grave list; I keep the roofs over them.

relations.name: Halvard Dunmore
relations.label: old neighbour
relations.note: He judges everyone's work, and mine is never quite right.

memories.gist: Mending the Cone's cracked band with Corvin Hollin, up on the scaffold in the cold, the heat coming through the brick.
The storm of last autumn took half the slates off Low Row; I worked three days without sleep and still could not save every roof.
Cora brought flowers to the graves on the Crown after the fever winter, and I built the little glass frames for them.
The first time I took slates from the shell of Mid Row 3, I felt like a thief, but the roof I patched that day has never leaked.
A game of counters at the Marver where I nearly beat Aldous Quill, and he said I had a good eye for a wall but not for a board.

stances.why: I have seen what damp does to a family, and I will not have it in my town.
A favour is a debt, and I keep my debts straight, even if others do not.
Nobody lives there, and a slate in use is better than a slate in a ruin.
Without the Cone there is no glass, and without glass there is no town; I mended its band and I would do it again.
She works as hard as I do, and the flowers are the only thing she asks for.

Cora Stannard.narrative: I grow flowers in a corner of glasshouse 4, and I bring them to the graves on the Crown. Oswin Greave, the head grower, wants the corner back for food, and I know he has a point, but the flowers are mine and they are for the dead. Gwil is my husband, and he keeps the roofs over us all. I spend my evenings at the wash-house wall with Greta and Elke, where the talk is warm and the Cone keeps us so.
goals: Keep my flower corner in glasshouse 4
Bring flowers to every grave on the Crown that wants them
See Gwil less tired and less worried about roofs
Grow a blue flower that will live through the winter
pastimes: Sitting at the wash-house wall with Greta and Elke
Walking the Crown to visit the graves
Cora Stannard.calling: I love to see a flower open where there was only grey, and to put it in the hands of someone who misses the dead.
Cora Stannard.mood: Gentle but stubborn; the flowers will stay.

relations.name: Gwil Stannard
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He works himself to the bone for the town, and I try to keep him warm.

relations.name: Oswin Greave
relations.label: head grower
relations.note: He wants my corner, but he has never said a word about the graves.

relations.name: Elke Greave
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We sit at the wash-house wall and put the town to rights.

relations.name: Greta Dunmore
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She hears everything and tells me most of it.

relations.name: Suri Greave
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She is expecting, and I bring her flowers to cheer her.

relations.name: Mirren Quill
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She laid out my mother, and she does it with kindness.

relations.name: Benedikt Orme
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: He keeps the grave list, and I keep the graves looking loved.

relations.name: Tamsin Hollin
relations.label: glazier
relations.note: She mends the glasshouses, and I hope she remembers my corner when she does.

memories.gist: The fever winter: I lost my mother and brought flowers to her grave every day until the frost killed them.
Oswin Greave told me the corner of glasshouse 4 could be better used for greens, and I said nothing but went home and cried.
The first flower I ever grew in the corner was a small yellow thing that Jory Greave's tree shaded; I moved it and it thrived.
A wash-house evening with Greta and Elke when we laughed until the Cone's shift changed and the night watch came on.
Gwil built me a little glass frame for the graves, and it has kept the wind off the flowers ever since.

stances.why: The graves on the Crown are all we have of the people we lost, and they should not be bare.
I have tended it for years, and Oswin has the rest of the Ladder.
I bring flowers to the sick and the sad, because someone did it for me.
It is warm and the talk is good, and you hear the truth there before anywhere else.
I do not understand the glass, but I know the Cone's wall keeps my evenings pleasant.
